title: Hosted API evolution: surface matrix, scope-matrix, and launch acceptance
creator: Ava Patel
summary: This ticket defines the product requirements, scope decisions, and launch acceptance for the next evolution of Redwood Hosted API endpoints. We unify behavioral contracts across chat/completions/embeddings/rerank with a surface matrix, specify migration and backward-compatibility constraints, and provide an operational launch checklist focused on SLOs, quality gates, and cost guardrails.
background: Multiple teams have independently iterated on hostable inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Customers report inconsistent behavior across endpoints (streaming semantics, structured output, error codes) and engineers maintain separate compatibility layers. This PRD aims to consolidate the behavioral surface and provide clear acceptance criteria so client SDKs and partner integrations face minimal surprises during rollout.
goals:
- Define a single canonical surface matrix for hosted endpoints covering request/response shape, streaming, tool-calling hooks, and error semantics.
- Lock scope for 2025.03 release: minimal breaking changes, explicit migration paths for next-major flags.
- Set measurable acceptance criteria (SLOs, quality regression thresholds, cost/per-token guardrails).
- Provide rollout and rollback playbook including canary metrics and automated fallback to compatible model variants.
scope_in:
- Behavioral contract definitions for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank.
- Streaming API contract and SDK compatibility notes (JS/Go/Python).
- Structured output and function-calling baseline grammar.
- Acceptance test harness (eval sets for chat and rerank).
- Canary rollout plan and monitoring dashboard templates.
- Migration recommendations for customers with pinned model versions.
scope_out:
- New multimodal endpoint types (image/video) — defer to Q3.
- Deep model-retraining or model architecture changes — handled in model-onboarding PRD.
- Major SDK language rework beyond compatibility shims (address in separate SDK roadmap ticket).
requirements:
1) Surface matrix document must list exact request fields and server behaviors for each endpoint kind; examples for legacy and new clients must be included.
2) Streaming: server-to-client stream must preserve chunk ordering; 'done' sentinel semantics must match existing JS SDK (see link).
3) Function/tool calling: the hosted API will expose a 'tools' array in responses when applicable; default behavior is non-blocking.
4) Error taxonomy: classify errors as transient, throttling, deterministic validation, or capacity-fallback; map to status codes and headers.
5) Backwards compatibility: any breaking change requires a runtime flag and 30-day migration window; SDKs must include opt-in flags before GA.
6) Quality gates: chat response pass rate >= 98% on gold prompt set (no hallucination > 2% as measured by eval harness).
7) SLOs: P50 latency <= 40ms for short completions (<128 tokens) and 99.9% availability for the new host surface during canary and GA.
8) Cost guardrails: autoscaling and batching defaults must preserve unit-cost within +10% vs baseline for standard workloads.
9) Telemetry: token-level cost and latency breakdown must be emitted per request and visible in console.
10) Rollback: automated routing policy must allow fallback to pre-2025.03 compatible model variant within 60s of detected regression.
acceptance_criteria:
- Surface matrix published and linked from console docs (internal doc link).
- JSON/HTTP contract tests passing in CI: 100% green on canonical examples.
- End-to-end integration tests: JS, Python SDKs validated against canary cluster with no regressions.
- Eval harness results: chat gold set pass rate >= 98%; rerank top-k accuracy within 1% of baseline.
- Monitoring: dashboards showing P50/P95/P99 latency, error taxonomy, and per-route token cost.
- Canary run: 72h with customer traffic slice >= 0.5% and no P1 regressions.
- Rollout automation: route policy can switch traffic away from new surface in under 60s.
- Backcompat shims: runtime flag works and SDK opt-in demonstrated with sample app.
- Security review completed and signed off by Security team.
- Docs and SDK changelog published and communication plan shared with top 50 customers.
rollout_plan:
1) Internal dev canary (ENG-only) for 48h — validate contract tests and telemetry.
2) Gradual external canary: 0.1% -> 0.5% -> 2% over 72 hours, with automated quality checks at each step.
3) Expand to 10% over 24h if metrics stable.
4) GA only after 7-day observational window post-10% with no major regressions.
5) Post-GA: monitor customer migration and provide migration-runbook office hours for two weeks.

Automations: automated rollback triggers on regression thresholds (chat eval failure > 1% over 30m, error-rate spike > 0.5%).
launch_checklist: API surface matrix doc published and linked in Console docs
Contract test suite merged and green in main branch
SDK compatibility shims released (JS/Python/Go) with samples
Eval harness for chat & rerank executed; results attached
Canary cluster provisioned and telemetry flows validated
Monitoring dashboards created and runbook documented
Security review completed and remediation items closed
Customer comms drafted and top-50 customers notified of migration window
Billing/usage alarms configured to detect cost spikes during rollout
open_questions: Can we standardize the 'function calling' signal across chat and completions without breaking current partners?
What guardrails do we need for rerank to prevent query amplification cost regressions?
Is the 30-day migration window sufficient for enterprise customers on Dedicated plans?
Do we expose an explicit 'compatibility' header for clients to opt into legacy semantics?
decisions: Adopt unified streaming 'chunk+done' sentinel matching current JS SDK to reduce client changes (made 2025-02-20).
Require a runtime flag for any behavior that differs from Feb-2025 contracts (policy approved 2025-02-25).
Canary thresholds: require no more than 1% absolute increase in chat hallucination rate vs baseline during canary (approved 2025-02-28).
